newsitem.title: USA: Delta rocket launches from Cape Canaveral.
newsitem.headline: Delta rocket launches from Cape Canaveral.

text.p: A Delta II rocket carried a Norwegian communication satellite safely into Earth orbit on Tuesday, in the first blastoff of one of the unmanned commercial spacecraft from Cape Canaveral since a Delta II exploded there shortly after liftoff in January.
The three-stage McDonnell Douglas Corp blasted off from the Cape Canaveral Air Station at 6:39 p.m. EDT (2239 GMT), the beginning of one of two potential launch windows available on Tuesday night.
The liftoff had been postponed from Sunday and then Monday because of bad weather, but mission control gave the go ahead to launch on Tuesday evening despite lightly gray skies.
The $150 million mission carried a Thor II communication satellite owned by Telenor International of Oslo, Norway, and built by Hughes Space and Communications Company, of El Segundo, California.
The satellite is designed to add up to 75 channels to Scandinavian television, company officials said.

On Jan. 17, an identical Delta II rocket exploded just seconds after clearing the launch tower, raining debris over the launch complex and sending a cloud of noxious gas spreading along Floridas east coast.

The explosion, the first in more than 300 missions, did $22 million in damage to the launch complex but caused no severe casualties. An investigation traced it to a cracked casing in one of Delta's solid rocket boosters, though the cause of that crack was never determined, said Ann Toulouse, director of communication for McDonnell Douglas.
On May 5, a Delta successfully launched from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California.
